question: Is God warlike or peaceful?
summary: Exodus 15:3 calls YHWH "a man of war" and Psalms 18:34 and 144:1 describe YHWH as the one who teaches hands to war and fingers to fight. The New Testament, by contrast, repeatedly titles God "the God of peace" (Rom 15:33, 16:20, 2 Cor 13:11, 1 Thess 5:23, Heb 13:20) and declares God is "not the author of confusion but of peace" (1 Cor 14:33). The contradiction is between a martial YHWH who trains warriors and a peaceful God who authors shalom.

reconcile.connective: The commentators read the martial titles as God acting in defense and judgment within history, not as a violent essence at odds with his peaceful character.

discrepancy.connective: The sharpest form of the objection is pressed by Marcion of Sinope, who argued the warlike creator-God of the Hebrew scriptures could not be the compassionate God of peace proclaimed by Jesus, and so must be a different deity.

skeptic.name: Marcion of Sinope
skeptic.attribution: Marcion of Sinope (d. c. 160), Antitheses (c. 144), reconstructed from Tertullian's Adversus Marcionem

pd_work.author: Tertullian
pd_work.note: Tertullian's five books answer Marcion's exact charge, defending the warlike Creator of the Old Testament as the one God who is also the God of peace, against the claim that the two cannot be the same deity.

link.title: CARM: Is the Lord a God of peace or of war? He is both
link.note: live apologetic treatment reading the martial titles in their deliverance/judgment context alongside God's peaceful nature

excerpts.excerpt_text: The Lord is a warrior: He will aggressively defend his own. He is not an oppressor, nor does he fight for the love of violence.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly distinguishes God's martial action (defending his people) from violence/oppression, harmonizing the warrior title with a non-violent character.
excerpts.source_note_text: 15:3 The Lord is a warrior: He will aggressively defend his own. He is not an oppressor, nor does he fight for the love of violence. But when his people are helpless before the enemy, whether external or internal, they can know that Yahweh, “He Who Is,” is their defender (Isa 59:15-19; 63:1-6; Rev 11:17-18). Regarding the name Yahweh, see study note on Exod 3:15.
